Preface to the second edition
I am very pleased that this alternative introduction to theoretical computer science has been so well received by colleagues and students. First of all, I would like to sincerely thank everyone who took the time to express their opinions about the book, as well as suggestions for improvements and extensions. I wrote this book with care because I knew that its content surpasses the framework of traditional concepts of the fundamentals of theoretical computer science. Therefore, I feared that many colleagues would regard it as a violation of the predominantly accepted representations of computer science fundamentals in undergraduate studies. Besides the many positive comments that alleviated my concerns, I found it most gratifying (as a real confirmation of the book's concept) that readers predominantly wished for the expansion into non-classical areas such as randomization and communication. I gladly accepted this challenge and have attempted to address it right away.
